units.text: INT. FAN - CONTINUOUS
Tries to open it , but fails .
Sees paper knife on bureau , and with it cuts cover from book .
Begins to start at the first page .
‘Mrs. Erlynne—£600—Mrs. Erlynne—£700—Mrs. Erlynne—£400.’ Oh! it is true! It is true! How horrible!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Throws book on floor .
Enter LORD WINDERMERE C.
Well, dear, has the fan been sent home yet?
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Going R.C. Sees book .
Margaret, you have cut open my bank book. You have no right to do such a thing!
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: You think it wrong that you are found out, don’t you?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: I think it wrong that a wife should spy on her husband.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: I did not spy on you. I never knew of this woman’s existence till half an hour ago. Some one who pitied me was kind enough to tell me what every one in London knows already—your daily visits to Curzon Street, your mad infatuation, the monstrous sums of money you squander on this infamous woman!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Crossing L.
Margaret! don’t talk like that of Mrs. Erlynne, you don’t know how unjust it is!
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Turning to him .
You are very jealous of Mrs. Erlynne’s honour. I wish you had been as jealous of mine.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Your honour is untouched, Margaret. You don’t think for a moment that—
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Puts book back into desk .

I think that you spend your money strangely. That is all. Oh, don’t imagine I mind about the money. As far as I am concerned, you may squander everything we have. But what I do mind is that you who have loved me, you who have taught me to love you, should pass from the love that is given to the love that is bought. Oh, it’s horrible!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Sits on sofa .

And it is I who feel degraded! you don’t feel anything. I feel stained, utterly stained. You can’t realise how hideous the last six months seems to me now—every kiss you have given me is tainted in my memory.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Crossing to her .
Don’t say that, Margaret. I never loved any one in the whole world but you.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Rises .
Who is this woman, then? Why do you take a house for her?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: I did not take a house for her.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: You gave her the money to do it, which is the same thing.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Margaret, as far as I have known Mrs. Erlynne—
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Is there a Mr. Erlynne—or is he a myth?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Her husband died many years ago. She is alone in the world.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: No relations?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: A pause .
None.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Rather curious, isn’t it?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: L.C.
Margaret, I was saying to you—and I beg you to listen to me—that as far as I have known Mrs. Erlynne, she has conducted herself well. If years ago—
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Oh!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Crossing R.C.
I don’t want details about her life!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: I am not going to give you any details about her life. I tell you simply this—Mrs. Erlynne was once honoured, loved, respected. She was well born, she had position—she lost everything—threw it away, if you like. That makes it all the more bitter. Misfortunes one can endure—they come from outside, they are accidents. But to suffer for one’s own faults—ah!—there is the sting of life. It was twenty years ago, too. She was little more than a girl then. She had been a wife for even less time than you have.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: I am not interested in her—and—you should not mention this woman and me in the same breath. It is an error of taste.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Sitting R. at desk .
Margaret, you could save this woman. She wants to get back into society, and she wants you to help her.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Crossing to her .
Me!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Yes, you.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: How impertinent of her!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE
